summary: Ages 7-8 build three-digit place value by assembling numbers in a hundreds|tens|ones (H|T|O) layout with base-ten materials, keeping the concrete build, the number name, and the expanded form (300+60+2) synchronised. A central focus is the placeholder zero: internal and trailing zeros (706, 350, 300) are where three-digit place value commonly breaks down, so learners build, partition, and explain why 706 is not 76. Includes arrow/place-value cards, a static reference anchor, two-tier checks with zero traps, and a 'detective' dialogue supplement.
misconceptions: Concatenation: writing 300 + 60 + 2 as 30062, or reading digits separately.
Mishandling internal zeros — writing 'seven hundred and six' as 76 or 7006.
Assigning the wrong place value (thinking the 3 in 362 means 3, not 300).
Losing the placeholder: dropping the 0 in 706 or 350.
Transposition of the spoken order vs written columns in larger numbers.

activities.title: H|T|O exchange bench: build, name, expand
steps: Set up three labelled columns: Hundreds | Tens | Ones.
Build 362 by placing 3 hundred-flats, 6 ten-rods and 2 ones-cubes into the matching columns.
Say the number name aloud ('three hundred and sixty-two') and write the expanded form 300 + 60 + 2.
Now empty the tens column (remove all 6 rods) and read the new number: 3 hundreds, 0 tens, 2 ones = 302. State what the 0 in the tens place means.
Work in reverse: 'Build seven hundred and six.' Leave the tens column empty and write 706, 700 + 0 + 6.
Build and contrast 76, 706 and 760 side by side; say how the columns differ.
Partition the same number more than one way, e.g. 362 = 300 + 60 + 2, 362 = 300 + 62, 362 = 340 + 22, 362 = 250 + 112.
activities.insight: Each column shows how many hundreds, tens or ones a digit counts, so a digit's value depends on its place; a 0 marks an empty place that still must be held, which is why 706 (7 hundreds, 0 tens, 6 ones) is not 76.

activities.title: Arrow/place-value cards: overlay and pull apart
steps: Take place-value (arrow) cards 300, 60 and 2 and overlay them so the smaller cards cover the trailing zeros of the larger, forming 362.
Pull the cards apart to recover the expanded form 300 + 60 + 2.
Repeat with a number containing an internal zero: overlay 700 and 6 to form 706, and notice no tens card is used — the tens place stays 0.
Say which zeros were hidden under which cards.
activities.insight: The expanded form and the compact numeral are two views of the same number; the trailing zeros inside 300 and 60 are hidden when cards overlap, and a missing card leaves a placeholder 0.

activities.title: Static reference anchor (labelled 362 and 706)
steps: Study a labelled picture of 362 built from flats, rods and cubes; for each digit, name its value (3 → 300, 6 → 60, 2 → 2).
Use a companion 706 anchor: open the 'why the 0?' note and read that there are no tens, but the place must be held.
Use these as a reference wall while doing the build and partition tasks.
activities.insight: A clearly labelled fixed example links each digit to its quantity and names the role of the placeholder zero, giving a stable picture to return to.

activities.title: Place-value detective: explain the zero
steps: A character keeps 'losing the zero' and reads 706 as 76.
Explain to the character what the 0 is doing and why 706 and 76 are different numbers.
Challenge the character with your own trap, e.g. ask how 350 differs from 35.
activities.insight: Articulating why a placeholder is needed consolidates the idea and surfaces whether the learner truly treats 0 as marking an empty place.

activities.title: Two-tier checks with zero traps
steps: Answer value-of-digit items: 'What is the 3 in 362 worth?' (300).
Match a built representation to its numeral, including 706 and 350 zero traps.
For each answer, give a reason: why is 706 different from 76 — what is the 0 doing?
Diagnostic: write 706 and explain what each digit is worth, what the 0 is doing, and how you know.
activities.insight: Once a number is built, learners can be checked on whether they read digits by place, handle the placeholder zero, and partition flexibly; the reason tier reveals whether the structure is understood or digits are read at face value.

checkQuestion: Write 706. Ask: 'What is each digit worth here — and what is the 0 doing? How do you know?'
checkAnswer: 7 hundreds (700), 0 tens, 6 ones. The 0 shows there are no tens and holds the tens place so the 7 stays in the hundreds.
